help.page.tactics.text:
# Tactics
The hero follows a list of rules on screen 2. Each rule is:
  when (one or two conditions) → do (an action, on a target) → until (an exit).
Every step the list is checked from the top. A rule that can't act right now (no mana, no potions, no target, ability not learned yet) is skipped and the next one is checked.

# Actions and behaviors
Actions take one step: potion, second wind, healing, blessing, attack and the spells. "Spells (auto)" picks the mage's spell the way the hero always did.
Every number can be compared with <, >, ≤ or ≥. The editor only offers what the hero's class can use. Behaviors keep going until their exit: Flee, Hunt and Retreat. Walking the floor follows the expedition mode: with no behavior active, the hero explores or descends as the mode says.

# Priority
A rule higher on the list always takes over from the active behavior; a lower one waits for it to stop. Only actions above the active behavior can run.

# Exits
  while it holds     stops when the conditions stop holding (default)
  until a condition  for example Flee until HP ≥ 50%
  for some seconds   stops after that time
  until done         no monster in sight
After stopping by time or by a condition, the rule waits for its conditions to clear before it can start again.

# Examples
  HP < 30% → Flee, until done
  enemies in sight ≥ 3 → Flee
  finished floor ≥ 15 → Retreat (returns after finishing floor 15)
"finished floor" only works with Retreat: it is checked right before the hero goes down the >.

# Default
The default list is how the hero always played, without drinking a potion before a hit that could kill: the hero never knows a hit would kill him. Restore default tactics brings it back.
help.classes.intro: Each class only uses certain weapons and armor: warrior and cleric use swords and maces; mage uses staves; rogue uses daggers. Abilities unlock at the level shown; the ones that cost MP are spells.
help.page.how.text:
# Expedition
The hero leaves town, goes down floor by floor and comes back on its own. You don't control the steps: you set up the expedition on screen 2 and spend gold in town (screen 1).

# What the hero does each step
One action per step, decided by the tactics (screen 2, Tactics): the rules are checked from the top and the first one that applies wins. By default:
  1. Heals if needed: second wind, healing spell or potion.
  2. Fights the adjacent monster (the mage also attacks from range).
  3. Walks to the most important goal:
     visible monster › item it wants › stairs > (descend mode) › unexplored area › boss or stairs >.
The ▸ line above the log shows the current goal. See the Tactics page.

# Combat
One round per second; the first one plays at walking pace. Speed decides who strikes first and grants extra attacks. Heroes and monsters follow the same DEX rule:
  Miss      20% − 0.5% per DEX (at least 5%). The cleric's blessing halves it.
  Critical  0.5% per DEX (at most 25%), double damage. Adds up with item critical.
Spells never miss.

# Retreat
By default the hero returns to town when the bag is full or when it has no potions and low HP; each one is a Retreat rule in the tactics, and you can change them or add others (like the last floor). Pressing r also sends it back. While retreating it walks to the stairs < and only the rules above the retreat still run (healing, by default); it only attacks if a monster blocks the only path.

# In town
Gold found ($ piles and slain monsters) is stored. The bag is sold for its items' value (plus 20% of what was spent at the blacksmith), or goes to the chest with "Sell loot on return" off. Legendaries are never sold on their own: they always go to the chest and are only sold with x and a confirmation. Blacksmith, training, shop and chest only work while the hero is in town.

# Death
Loses 75% of the gold and all items found on the expedition. Keeps level, XP, potions and the gear it left with.

# Bosses
Every 10 floors a boss guards the stairs. It sleeps until the hero gets close. The hero can't tell whether it will win: it fights to the end (or until the no-potions low-HP rule kicks in). Once defeated, it drops a rare, epic or legendary item and unlocks a shortcut to start deeper.

# Auto-expedition (a)
When on, the hero rests a few seconds in town and sets out again on its own.

# While closed
When you reopen the game, it simulates the time it was closed (up to 12 hours) and shows a summary.
help.page.attrs.text:
# Attributes
  STR  Strength: melee damage for the warrior, mage and cleric.
  DEX  Dexterity: speed (explores faster and acts more often in combat), accuracy, critical hits and rogue damage. Monsters have DEX too.
  INT  Intelligence: spell damage, mana and mana recovery (mage and cleric).
  CON  Constitution: max HP.
Every hero gains attributes on level up. Training in town adds permanent points; the description line shows the effect before you buy.

# Hero numbers
  Attack     weapon + the class damage attribute.
  Defense    armor + helmet + shield + level. Reduces damage taken. Armor, helmet and shield also add half of their defense as max HP.
  Speed      boots + DEX. The /s value is how many steps per second while exploring.
  Spell      damage of the best spell (mage and cleric).
  MP         mana; spells spend it and it comes back each step (faster with INT).
  Potion     heals 35% of max HP (more with the potions + effect).

# Monsters
They get stronger every floor. Each kind has its own DEX (bat, wolf and werewolf are agile), which rises 1 every 2 floors; bosses have more.

# Items
Each item has a main attribute, which depends on its type:
  Weapon                    Attack
  Armor, helmet and shield  Defense
  Boots                     Speed
Rare, epic and legendary items also have effects (see below).
The blacksmith only improves the main attribute.
Sell price: an item is worth gold piles ($) of its floor. Common is worth 1 pile, magic 2, rare 3, epic 4 and legendary 5. Each effect adds up to 1 more pile.

# Item rarity
Common (white) › Magic (blue) › Rare (green) › Epic (purple) › Legendary (orange). On the same floor, a higher rarity is never weaker. Rares have 1 special effect, epics 2 and legendaries 3. Effect values do not depend on rarity.

# Item effects
They show in the item name. The same effect on different items adds up, to a cap on the total.
  life steal  The hero recovers this % of all damage it deals, spells included (5–15%; up to 30% total).
  crit        Adds this % to the critical chance that comes from DEX (5–15%; up to 75% total).
  HP +        Raises max HP by this % (5–15%; up to 50% total).
  gold +      More gold from $ piles and slain monsters (10–30%; up to 100% total).
  potions +   Each potion heals this % more of max HP, on top of the usual 35% (10–30%; up to 60% total).
  XP +        More XP per slain monster (5–15%; up to 50% total).
help.rarity: Items: white common, blue magic, green rare, purple epic, orange legendary
prep.effects.desc: Full: lamp, damage numbers, shake and sparkles. Subtle: steady lamp, numbers and flash, no shake or sparkles. Off: plain map.

ability.power_strike.desc: Every 4 attacks, a blow that deals double damage.
ability.second_wind.desc: Below 30% HP, heals 40% of max HP. Once per expedition.
ability.whirlwind.desc: With 2 or more monsters adjacent, the power strike hits all of them.
ability.sneak_attack.desc: Triple damage against a monster that is asleep or still unhurt.
ability.dodge.desc: Chance to dodge blows: 3% per DEX, up to 35%.
ability.treasure_nose.desc: Gold piles 50% bigger and a chance of one extra item per floor.
spell.magic_missile.desc: Ranged attack, up to 5 tiles. Damage: 4 + INT + weapon.
spell.sleep.desc: With 2 or more awake monsters nearby, puts one to sleep for 6 rounds (boss: 2).
spell.fireball.desc: Hits the target and anyone next to it, when there are 2 or more. Damage: 4 + INT + weapon.
spell.blink.desc: When surrounded and below 35% HP, teleports to the spot farthest from monsters.
spell.frost_ray.desc: Against a monster faster than the hero: 6 + INT + weapon damage and 5 rounds of slow.
spell.heal.desc: Below the potion HP threshold, heals 35% of max HP + INT.
spell.bless.desc: In combat, for 8 rounds: half the miss chance and +3 Defense.
spell.turn_undead.desc: Triple damage against the undead (zombie, skeleton and the Lich).
tactics.field.op.desc: How the number is compared: < less, > more, ≤ at most, ≥ at least.
gambit.do.potion.desc: Drinks a potion. Skipped at full HP or with none left.
gambit.do.second_wind.desc: Warrior ability: a big heal at low HP, once per expedition.
gambit.do.bless.desc: Cleric spell: blesses the hero for a few rounds.
gambit.do.attack.desc: Hits a monster next to the hero.
gambit.do.spells.desc: Mage: picks the spell the way the hero always did (blink, sleep, fireball, frost ray or magic missile).
gambit.do.missile.desc: Mage spell: hits a monster in range.
gambit.do.fireball.desc: Mage spell: hits the target and everything next to it.
gambit.do.frost.desc: Mage spell: hurts and slows the target.
gambit.do.sleep.desc: Mage spell: puts the target to sleep.
gambit.do.blink.desc: Mage spell: jumps away from the monsters next to the hero.
gambit.do.idle.desc: Stands still: mana comes back, but monsters can still hit.
gambit.do.flee.desc: Runs from the awake monsters in sight by walking distance, heading for doors, corridors and other rooms instead of corners.
gambit.do.hunt.desc: Goes after a monster in sight and attacks it.
gambit.do.explore.desc: Plays like always: chases what it sees, picks up loot, explores and goes down.
gambit.do.descend.desc: Like Explore, but takes the stairs > as soon as it sees them.
gambit.do.retreat.desc: Walks back to the exit < and goes to town. Only rules above it still run.
tactics.rule.desc: Every step the hero checks the rules from the top and does the first one that applies; a rule that can't act (no mana, no target) is skipped. Enter edits.
tactics.add.desc: Adds a rule at the bottom and opens it.
tactics.reset.desc: Goes back to the rules the hero plays with by default.
confirm.tactics_discard: Discard the changes to the rule?
tactics.field.if.desc: First condition. —: the rule always applies.
tactics.field.and.desc: Second condition; both must hold. —: no second condition.
tactics.field.n.desc: The number of the condition above.
tactics.field.exit.desc: When a behavior stops: while its condition holds, until another condition, after some seconds, or when it is done (no monster in sight). A rule higher on the list always takes over.
tactics.field.until.desc: The behavior stops when this holds.
tactics.up.desc: Rules higher on the list win.
tactics.down.desc: Rules lower on the list only run when the ones above don't apply.
tactics.done.desc: Applies the changes and goes back to the list. Until then the hero follows the old rule.
tactics.cancel.desc: Discards the changes and goes back to the list.
touch.hint: tap to select · tap again to use
prep.nerd.desc: Shows tab 5 with every balance number and what it changes. Doesn't change the game.
nerd.keys: ↑↓ choose · read only: the numbers the game uses right now
nerd.damage.desc: Every hit rolls 80–120% of the attack and subtracts half the target's defense, at least 1. Defense matters a lot early and less once attack is far above it.
nerd.miss_base.desc: Chance that any attack misses before DEX. Higher = longer, swingier fights for everyone.
nerd.miss_per_dex.desc: Each DEX point of the attacker lowers its miss chance by this much. Makes DEX worth more for accurate fighters.
nerd.miss_min.desc: No amount of DEX lowers the miss chance below this. Higher = even strong attackers keep missing sometimes.
nerd.crit_per_dex.desc: Each DEX point gives this much chance of a critical hit (heroes and monsters). Item effects add on top.
nerd.crit_max.desc: Cap of the critical chance that DEX gives. Higher = high-DEX monsters and heroes burst much harder.
nerd.combat_round.desc: Real time of one combat step. Lower = fights end sooner, so more floors and loot per hour (online and offline).
nerd.monster_growth.desc: HP, attack, defense and XP of a monster grow by this share of its base for each floor below its first floor. The main difficulty curve of the dungeon.
nerd.monster_atk.desc: Extra multiplier on monster attack on top of the growth. The main knob for how hard monsters hit and how often the hero needs potions.
nerd.monster_dex.desc: A monster gains 1 DEX for every this many floors below its first floor: fewer misses and more criticals deep down.
nerd.monster_window.desc: Only the newest kinds unlocked on the floor can spawn. Lower = only the toughest kinds; higher = weak old kinds stay mixed in.
nerd.monster_count.desc: 3 + floor/2, between these limits. More monsters = more XP and gold per floor, but more damage taken and slower floors.
nerd.monster.value: HP %d Atk %d Def %d Spd %d XP %d DEX %d · floor %d+
nerd.monster.desc: Base stats on its first floor; deeper floors multiply them by the growth. Speed doesn't grow: above the hero's speed the monster acts first and attacks more often.
nerd.monster.undead: Undead: the cleric's Turn Undead deals triple damage to it.
nerd.boss_every.desc: A boss guards the > every this many floors and blocks the way down. Killing it drops a rare, epic or legendary item and unlocks a shortcut.
nerd.boss_hp.desc: The boss takes the strongest monster of the floor and multiplies its HP; each later boss multiplies more. The main reason bosses are milestones.
nerd.boss_atk.desc: Multiplier on the base monster's attack, growing with each boss. Higher = more hero deaths at floors 10, 20, 30…
nerd.boss_def.desc: Multiplier on the base monster's defense. Higher = weak weapons barely scratch the boss.
nerd.boss_xp.desc: Multiplier on the base monster's XP. Killing a boss is a big level jump.
nerd.boss_spd.desc: A boss is never slower than this. Faster than the hero = it acts first and attacks more than once per step.
nerd.boss_dex.desc: Extra DEX on top of the base monster: fewer misses and more criticals.
nerd.boss_wake.desc: The boss sleeps until the hero is this close (in tiles).
nerd.boss_epic.desc: Chance that the boss item is epic; if neither epic nor legendary, it is rare. Higher = farming bosses yields more strong gear.
nerd.boss_legendary.desc: Chance that the boss item is legendary. Higher = legendaries stop being pure floor luck.
nerd.hero_atk.desc: Attack every hero has before gear. Attack = this + weapon + the class damage attribute (STR, or DEX for the rogue). Matters most on the first floors.
nerd.hero_def.desc: Defense before gear. The hero also gets +1 defense every 2 levels. Each defense point cuts 0.5 damage from every hit taken.
nerd.hero_spd.desc: Speed = this + boots + DEX. Sets exploration pace and, in combat, who acts first and how often monsters attack (a monster attacks its speed ÷ hero speed times per step).
nerd.steps.desc: How many tiles per second the hero walks while exploring. Faster = more floors, loot and XP per hour, online and offline.
nerd.explore_dex.desc: DEX only counts this fraction toward exploration speed (it counts fully in combat). Keeps high-DEX heroes from racing through floors.
nerd.xp_next.desc: XP needed for the next level, multiplied for each level after. Higher growth = leveling slows down sooner and gear matters more than levels.
nerd.con_hp.desc: Max HP each CON point gives (training CON in town). The only way to buy HP directly.
nerd.armor_hp.desc: This share of the armor, helmet and shield defense is added to max HP. Lets gear keep the hero alive on deep floors.
nerd.start_potions.desc: Potions a new hero has. Potions are kept on death.
nerd.potion_heal.desc: Share of max HP a potion heals (item effects add on top). Higher = each potion saves more fights.
nerd.max_potions.desc: How many potions the hero carries. Caps how long an expedition can last.
nerd.death_gold.desc: Share of the expedition gold kept on death; the bag is lost. Higher = dying hurts less.
nerd.town_wait.desc: Time the hero waits in town between expeditions. Lower = more expeditions per hour.
nerd.offline_cap.desc: Most time simulated when the game is reopened. Time away beyond this is lost.
nerd.gold_piles.desc: How many gold piles a floor has. The main gold source besides selling loot.
nerd.gold_pile.desc: Average gold of a pile on floor 1, multiplied for each floor deeper. Each pile rolls 50–150% of it. Makes deep floors much richer.
nerd.gold_kill.desc: Each monster drops gold equal to its XP divided by this number (at least 1). It is the biggest source of gold.
nerd.items.desc: How many items lie on a floor. More = faster gear upgrades and a fuller bag.
nerd.potion_chance.desc: Chance a floor has a potion on the ground. Higher = expeditions last longer.
nerd.rarity_chance.desc: Chance each item found or sold in the shop is of this rarity. The shop never sells legendaries. Higher = stronger gear sooner.
nerd.item_base.weapon.desc: Attack of a common weapon by floor. Weapons grow faster than anything else; it's why STR is weak next to a new weapon.
nerd.item_base.armor.desc: Defense of a common medium armor by floor. Light and heavy are multiplied by their weight.
nerd.item_base.helmet.desc: Defense of a common helmet (shields are the same) by floor: half of an armor.
nerd.item_base.boots.desc: Speed of common boots by floor. Grows slowly and +1 per rarity step; boots don't roll the ±spread.
nerd.rarity_mult.desc: Multiplier on weapon, armor, helmet and shield bonus for this rarity.
nerd.weight.desc: Defense multiplier by armor weight. Classes that can wear heavy armor get more defense and HP.
nerd.item_spread.desc: Random spread of an item's bonus around its base. Higher = luckier and unluckier drops.
nerd.effects.desc: How many special effects rare, epic and legendary items roll. Each effect has the same range at any rarity.
nerd.effect.life_steal.desc: Heals this share of the damage dealt. Rolls a value in this range.
nerd.effect.crit.desc: Extra critical chance, on top of DEX. A critical deals double damage. Rolls a value in this range.
nerd.effect.vigor.desc: Raises max HP by this percent. Rolls a value in this range.
nerd.effect.gold_find.desc: More gold from piles and monsters. Rolls a value in this range.
nerd.effect.potion_boost.desc: Potions heal this much more of max HP. Rolls a value in this range.
nerd.effect.xp_boost.desc: More XP from every monster. Rolls a value in this range.
nerd.bag.desc: Bag slots of a new hero. A full bag sends the hero back to town, so it limits how deep an expedition goes.
nerd.bag_slots.desc: Slots each bag upgrade adds × how many upgrades exist.
nerd.bag_cost.desc: Price of the first bag upgrade, multiplied for each one after.
nerd.stash.desc: Items the town chest holds when loot selling is off.
nerd.shop_size.desc: Items the shop offers, rolled at the deepest floor reached.
nerd.shop_markup.desc: Shop price = item value × this. Higher = buying gear is a worse deal than finding it.
nerd.item_value.desc: Sell price = gold piles of the item's floor × this × (rarity + 1). The floor comes from the main attribute compared to what is normal for its type. Also drives shop prices.
nerd.effect_value: Value of each effect in piles
nerd.effect_value.desc: Each effect adds up to this many gold piles of the item's floor to the price, by its strength.
nerd.upgrade_refund.desc: Share of the gold spent at the blacksmith returned when that item is sold.
nerd.potion_price.desc: Gold for one potion in town.
nerd.potion_sell.desc: Gold for selling one extra potion.
nerd.upgrade.desc: Each blacksmith upgrade adds this fraction of the item's base as if it were common (at least 1). Rarity does not raise the gain.
nerd.upgrade_max.desc: How many upgrades each item takes. Higher = old items stay useful for longer.
nerd.upgrade_cost.desc: Price of an upgrade: value of the item's base as if it were common (multiplied by rarity, like the sell price) + 10, multiplied for each upgrade already done. Each one costs much more than the last.
nerd.train.desc: Price of the first training of this attribute, multiplied for each training after.
nerd.class.desc: Starting max HP, HP gained per level and the attributes the class starts with and gains every 2 levels.
nerd.mana.desc: Base max mana, max mana per INT point and extra mana per step per INT point. More mana = more spells per fight.
nerd.mana_regen.desc: Mana every caster recovers per step before INT.
nerd.power_strike.desc: The warrior's power strike (double damage) comes every this many attacks. Lower = more warrior damage.
nerd.second_wind.desc: HP percent below which the warrior's second wind fires, once per expedition.
nerd.second_wind_heal.desc: Share of max HP the second wind heals.
nerd.sneak.desc: Damage multiplier of the rogue's hit on a sleeping or unhurt monster.
nerd.dodge.desc: The rogue's chance to dodge a hit for each DEX point.
nerd.dodge_cap.desc: Cap of the rogue's dodge chance. Higher = the rogue gets very hard to kill.
nerd.nose_gold.desc: Gold pile multiplier for the rogue's treasure nose.
nerd.nose_item.desc: Chance treasure nose adds one extra item to each floor.
nerd.spell_range.desc: How far (in tiles) spells reach. Higher = the mage hits more before monsters close in.
nerd.spell_power.desc: Base attack of the spell; INT and the weapon bonus are added.
nerd.sleep_min.desc: Sleep is only cast on a monster above this HP percent, so it isn't wasted on one about to die.
nerd.sleep.desc: How long sleep keeps a normal monster out of the fight.
nerd.sleep_boss.desc: How long sleep lasts on a boss.
nerd.frost.desc: Rounds the frost ray halves a monster's speed.
nerd.blink.desc: HP percent below which the mage blinks away when surrounded.
nerd.heal.desc: Share of max HP the cleric's heal restores, plus INT.
nerd.bless.desc: How long the blessing lasts (half the miss chance and extra defense).
nerd.turn_undead.desc: Damage multiplier of the cleric against undead.
